title: Mistral OCR responses lack read, body, cardinality, and persistence bounds
summary: The Mistral OCR client has no effective read or overall deadline and no response-body ceiling before full JSON materialization. It then collects page and image data, decodes base64 content, and persists images before the CLI's response-acceptance check, allowing a connected remote peer to consume local memory, CPU, time, and disk.

severity.rationale: A remote adapter response is a realistic in-scope attacker source once an ordinary approved OCR request occurs. The path is bounded to availability and disk effects, and the required matrix maps medium impact plus high likelihood to medium.
severity.changeConditions: Severity would rise if a malicious response can reliably cause durable multi-scope outage or overwrite unrelated data; it would fall after effective deadlines, body/cardinality/decoded-byte limits, and a pre-persistence aggregate quota are enforced.

confidence.rationale: V5+V10. Exact source-to-sink trace shows full OCR JSON materialization followed by unbounded page/image expansion and pre-acceptance CAS writes. Cargo.lock pins ureq 2.12.1; local primary source defaults are connect=30s, read/write/overall=None, and into_json uses serde_json::from_reader without caller take. Four bounded network-free existing tests passed for image persistence and page-scoped request behavior.

taxonomy.category: uncontrolled resource consumption from remote response (CWE-400, CWE-770)

locations.role: OCR POST and full JSON materialization

codeEvidence.label: OCR response is fully materialized
codeEvidence.explanation: The authenticated OCR request reads the response through unrestricted `into_json()` and supplies no caller deadline or byte ceiling before materialization.

codeEvidence.label: Every page and image is collected and decoded
codeEvidence.code:
fn parse_ocr_response(value: Value, model_pin: &str) -> Result<OcrResponse> {
    let pages = value
        .get("pages")
        .and_then(Value::as_array)
        .ok_or_else(|| AdapterError::ContractViolation("OCR response missing pages".to_owned()))?
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(fallback_index, page)| parse_ocr_page(page, fallback_index))
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
    Ok(OcrResponse {
        pages,
        model_version_pin: value
            .get("model")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .unwrap_or(model_pin)
            .to_owned(),
    })
}

fn parse_ocr_page(value: &Value, fallback_index: usize) -> Result<OcrPage> {
    let images = value
        .get("images")
        .and_then(Value::as_array)
        .into_iter()
        .flatten()
        .map(parse_ocr_image)
        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
    Ok(OcrPage {
        index: value
            .get("index")
            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .map(|index| index as usize)
            .unwrap_or(fallback_index),
        markdown: value
            .get("markdown")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .unwrap_or_default()
            .to_owned(),
        images,
    })
}

fn parse_ocr_image(value: &Value) -> Result<OcrImage> {
    let raw_base64 = value
        .get("image_base64")
        .or_else(|| value.get("base64"))
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let (media_type, data) = split_data_uri(raw_base64);
    let bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD
        .decode(data)
        .map_err(|err| AdapterError::ContractViolation(err.to_string()))?;
codeEvidence.explanation: The parser collects all pages and images, clones markdown strings, and base64-decodes each remote image without cardinality or decoded-byte limits.

codeEvidence.label: Images persist before caller acceptance
codeEvidence.explanation: The adapter writes every parsed page image to the image store immediately after the OCR call, before returning the response to the CLI.

codeEvidence.label: CLI validates only after adapter completion
codeEvidence.explanation: The CLI's strict response validation runs only after the adapter has materialized the response and persisted images.

codeEvidence.label: Configured timeout is not threaded
codeEvidence.explanation: Configuration accepts only the documented default value but explicitly does not thread it into adapter HTTP transports, leaving no effective application deadline.

rootCause.summary: The OCR transport calls unrestricted `into_json()` without threading the configured timeout or a compressed/decompressed body ceiling. Parsed page, markdown, and image cardinalities and decoded bytes are also unbounded, and image persistence occurs inside the adapter before caller acceptance.

remediation: Use a shared bounded OCR transport with configured deadlines, compressed/decompressed body limits, page/markdown/image/decoded-byte limits, and a pre-persistence aggregate quota; retain the existing outbound input cap.

attackPath.summary: The operator configures and authorizes an online Mistral OCR operation for an eligible document. The configured remote service, proxy, or intermediary accepts the authenticated request and slow-streams or returns an oversized or highly expanded response. KCS reads and decompresses the complete JSON without a read or overall deadline or byte ceiling, then collects all pages, markdown, and images and decodes every base64 image. Images are persisted before the caller's acceptance check, allowing the remote peer to hang the command or consume substantial memory, CPU, and disk.

reachability.summary: outbound remote connection only; KCS has no public listener and the path begins after online-adapter approval
reachability.attacker: KCS uses the victim OS identity and configured Mistral credential; the untrusted remote peer controls response timing and content but gains no additional local identity
reachability.entrypoint: The operator configures and authorizes an online Mistral OCR operation for an eligible document.
reachability.preconditions: plausible: an eligible approved OCR operation reaches a connected peer that can control the response; no local privilege or private-store write is required
reachability.outcome: runtime memory, CPU, command availability, store-lock duration, and archive disk usage

impact.why: A remote adapter response is a realistic in-scope attacker source once an ordinary approved OCR request occurs. The path is bounded to availability and disk effects, and the required matrix maps medium impact plus high likelihood to medium.

likelihood.why: An operator-approved online OCR request is made. The configured service, proxy, or intermediary is faulty, compromised, or hostile. The response remains syntactically processable long enough to drive the unbounded sinks.

counterevidence: The outbound request body is bounded by effective_max_input_bytes on the shipped CLI path.
Later acceptance checks can reject bad semantic output, but run only after response allocation and image persistence.
A well-behaved provider ordinarily constrains responses, but the threat model treats provider behavior as untrusted.
limitations: No loopback timing/body measurement was run under the read-only/no-network constraint; exact code and pinned dependency defaults make this non-material to disposition.
No loopback slow-read or oversized-body measurement was retained; the exact resource constants remain unmeasured.

remediationTests: Use a local bounded fake transport to verify read/overall deadlines and compressed/decompressed body ceilings terminate slow or oversized responses.
Reject excessive page, markdown, image, and decoded-byte cardinality before any image-CAS write, while retaining valid bounded responses.
preventiveControls: online opt-in and current input-size check

Use a shared bounded OCR transport with configured deadlines, compressed/decompressed body limits, page/markdown/image/decoded-byte limits, and a pre-persistence aggregate quota; retain the existing outbound input cap.
